questions.question: How does the Digital India programme structure its objective of improving citizen access to government?
questions.explanation: The passage states the programme is organised around three pillars: digital infrastructure as a utility, governance and on-demand services, and digital empowerment.
questions.source_sentence: The programme is organised around three pillars: digital infrastructure as a utility available to every citizen, governance and on-demand services, and digital empowerment.

options.A: By mandating that all private companies provide free internet to rural areas
options.B: By replacing all physical government offices with automated kiosks
options.C: By focusing on digital infrastructure, on-demand governance services, and digital empowerment
options.D: By focusing exclusively on the development of the Unified Payments Interface

questions.question: What is the current status of the Digital India programme after a decade of operation?
questions.explanation: The passage notes that while it built major infrastructure like Aadhaar and UPI, gaps in areas like rural access and transparency persist.
questions.source_sentence: Independent assessments after a decade of launch credit it with building one of the world's largest "digital public infrastructure"—Aadhaar, the Unified Payments Interface, and several other platforms.

options.A: It has successfully established major digital public infrastructure, though significant challenges remain
options.B: It has fully resolved all issues regarding rural access and gender parity
options.C: It has been discontinued due to a lack of transparency and data protection
options.D: It has shifted its focus away from digital infrastructure to prioritize job creation

questions.question: What role does Digital India play regarding platforms like the Government e-Marketplace (GeM)?
questions.explanation: The passage describes Digital India as the umbrella under which the government promotes platforms like GeM.
questions.source_sentence: The programme has become the umbrella under which the Government of India has built and promoted state-run and state-backed digital platforms, including the Open Network for Digital Commerce and Government e-Marketplace.

options.B: It is a specific sub-component managed exclusively by the GeM team
options.C: It provides the funding for GeM but does not oversee its operations
options.D: It serves as the overarching framework for promoting state-backed digital platforms

variables.PASSAGE:
Digital India is a government of India programme that aims to deliver government services electronically, expand broadband connectivity to rural India, improve citizens' digital literacy, and expand digital inclusion. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched it on 1 July 2015; the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) primarily administers it, working alongside related programmes such as Bharat Broadband Network, Make in India, and Atmanirbhar Bharat.
The programme is organised around three pillars: digital infrastructure as a utility available to every citizen, governance and on-demand services, and digital empowerment. Independent assessments after a decade of launch credit it with building one of the world's largest "digital public infrastructure"—Aadhaar, the Unified Payments Interface, and several other platforms. Gaps in rural access, gender parity, data protection, and programme transparency persist.
The programme has become the umbrella under which the Government of India has built and promoted state-run and state-backed digital platforms, including the Open Network for Digital Commerce and Government e-Marketplace. At the launch of the program, several domestic and international companies promised to invest ₹4.5 lakh crore (equivalent to ₹7.4 trillion or US$79 billion in 2026), with Mukesh Ambani leading with a ₹2.5 lakh crore (equivalent to ₹4.1 trillion or US$44 billion in 2026) pledge. The programme was expected to create 18 lakh jobs
